description: HexLattice::from_rings builds a 2-ring lattice whose central tile [n_rings-1,n_rings-1] receives outer-ring element index 3 instead of the single inner-ring element. Confirmed for BOTH orientations at n_rings=2: with outer ring [10,11,12,13,14,15] and inner [42], universe_at(centre)=13 (=outer[3]) not 42; the inner element lands off-centre (e.g. X orientation puts it at [2,0]). The geometry methods (center_offset/get_indices/get_local_position/distance) are CORRECT — the bug is purely in the ring->tile fill walk (fill_lattice_x src/lattice.cpp:546, fill_lattice_y :598) and/or the outer-first flatten order from_rings feeds them. The existing 4-ring y notebook test did not catch it because every ring's first element AND the inner ring all share the value 1, so a mis-slotted centre still reads 1. NEEDS the canonical OpenMC src/lattice.cpp fill_lattice_x/y to diff against (not available on this build host) before fixing, per the crate's mirror-canonical-source rule. Found while adding op-6tz.31 (X round-trip test); that test and the new from_rings_3d test both deliberately avoid asserting intra-level fill placement.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: Fixed in 590b0e0. Root cause: from_rings/from_rings_3d fed outer-ring-first input to the row-order fill_lattice_x/y walk (spatial rows, not hex rings) → central element mis-placed onto an outer tile; the whole placement was a non-round-tripping permutation. Fix: geometry-derived placement (fill_level via ring_slots/tile_ring/tile_xy) — per hex-radius k, sort that ring's skewed tiles by planar angle (+x start, CCW) and map ring elements onto them; proven bijection over all hexagon tiles, so universe_at(get_indices(tile_centre)) round-trips. New tests ring_fill_round_trip_{x,y} + from_rings_3d_single_level_matches_2d; 158 lib + 27 notebook tests pass. CAVEAT: within-ring +x-start CCW angular convention is best-effort per OpenMC's 'each ring starts along +x' doc; a line-by-line diff vs openmc/lattice.py is still owed. Round-trip correctness + valid bijection verified; NOT claimed OpenMC-bit-identical.

title: outram-mc: fill_lattice_x/y misplace ring elements for small ring counts

description:
Maintainer report, 2026-08-13 (filed outside active hours; no code work done).

In the htgr_sim_v1 GUI schematic, the hot gas duct should connect correctly to the duct pipe at the BOTTOM RIGHT of the steam generator. It currently does not line up.

Scope when picked up during active hours:
- Locate the schematic layout code for htgr_sim_v1 (tampines example / digital-twin engine GUI components) and the anchor points used for the hot gas duct and the steam generator's bottom-right duct pipe.
- Fix the connection so the duct terminates on the SG duct-pipe port rather than floating / mis-aligned.
- Purely a schematic/visual routing fix; no plant physics change intended.
- Check the same anchor convention is not broken for the cold-leg / return duct while fixing it.

Related: op-szmi.5 (finish the GUI to CIET v2 standard), op-wqk.9.4 (schematic omits PipeVisual).

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
FIXED 2026-08-13. It was not a small offset.

ROOT CAUSE: SteamGeneratorVisual::draw_helical_coil paints its hot-gas nozzle as a stub on the vessel's BOTTOM RIGHT
(cx + 0.02w .. cx + 0.68w over y(0.925)..y(0.955)), feeding the bottom of the centre tube the hot helium rises through.
The schematic ignored that and routed the duct to sg_rect().left() + 1.0 at reactor.top() + 0.66 * reactor.height() --
an elevation set by the REACTOR's plenum, on the SG's blank LEFT flank. Measured miss: 105.31 pt horizontal,
130.17 pt vertical. A hardcoded endpoint never tied to the SG's own geometry.

SEARCH: no generic port/anchor/router helper exists in the engine. The convention that does exist is local to
schematic.rs -- reactor_rect()/sg_rect()/pump_discharge() reproduce each widget's own letterbox and nozzle fractions.
The three other SG nozzles already followed it; only the hot duct did not. Followed the existing convention rather than
inventing a second one. HelicalCoil has exactly one consumer, so the shared widget was not touched.

FIX: new derived anchors in schematic.rs -- reactor_duct_nozzle() and an SgNozzles struct (cold_gas_out, steam_out,
feed_in, hot_gas_in) computed from sg_rect() with the artwork's own fractions, plus hot_gas_duct_path() -> [Pos2; 6].
The stub points AWAY from the reactor so the duct cannot be straight: cross-vessel leg at plenum elevation, down clear
of the cold-return riser, under the feedwater header, up past the SG, back into the nozzle from the right. Three magic
numbers (370.0, 390.0, 585.0) hoisted into named constants; NOZZLE_SEAM_OVERLAP = 3.0 for the joint.

COLD LEG CHECKED AND UNCHANGED, as requested: the_cold_leg_anchors_are_unchanged pins cold gas out (514.955, 175.828),
steam out (621.261, 197.207), feedwater in (514.955, 516.865) -- identical to the previous inline expressions.

VERIFIED NUMERICALLY (6 new tests): nozzle tip (621.261, 534.171), duct end (618.261, 534.171) -- 3.000 pt inboard,
0.000 pt off centreline; all 5 legs axis-aligned; no leg intersects the SG rect inflated by half the pipe width
(closest 46.40 pt below, 48.22 pt right).

NOT VERIFIED VISUALLY -- headless, no display. ONE DELIBERATE COMPROMISE for the maintainer to eyeball: the duct riser
CROSSES THE FEEDWATER HEADER at (653.3, 585.0). It is the only run-over-run crossing in the schematic and is
unavoidable -- the header sweeps the plant's full width at an elevation the duct must climb through. Documented in the
code, deliberately not asserted against.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
VISUALLY CONFIRMED BY THE MAINTAINER, 2026-08-13: 'hot gas duct looks right.'

This closes the one gap the fix could not verify itself. The numeric tests pinned the endpoint to the nozzle
(3.000 pt inboard, 0.000 pt off centreline) and proved the legs axis-aligned and clear of the SG rect, but nothing
automated could judge whether the routing READS correctly on screen. A human has now looked at it.

The deliberate compromise recorded on this bead -- the duct riser crossing the feedwater header at (653.3, 585.0),
the only run-over-run crossing in the schematic -- is accepted as part of that sign-off.

title: htgr_sim_v1 schematic: hot gas duct does not connect to the steam generator's bottom-right duct pipe

description:
FLAGGED 2026-08-05 during the op-6sl.7 validation-case work. NOT CONFIRMED — logged as a hypothesis to check, not a finding.

Search summaries of the abstract of Northwood, London & Bahen (1975), 'Elastic constants of zirconium alloys', J. Nucl. Mater. 55(3) 299-310, DOI 10.1016/0022-3115(75)90071-9, ADS 1975JNuM...55..299N, state that MEASURED Poisson's ratio DECREASES with temperature for Zircaloy-2.

The ported MATPRO correlation pair gives nu INCREASING with temperature throughout the alpha range — that is the whole mechanism by which it crosses 0.5 at 1354.84 K.

IF THE ABSTRACT IS RIGHT, this is a wrong-SIGN error across the entire alpha range, which is far more serious than the crossover the parent bead records. The crossover would then be a symptom rather than the disease.

THE PAPER WAS NOT READ. Every literature host was blocked by this container's egress policy — osti.gov, nrc.gov, pnnl.gov, digital.library.unt.edu, inis.iaea.org, sciencedirect.com, link.aps.org, doi.org, arxiv.org all refused at CONNECT with 403, and WebFetch is blocked session-wide. So this rests on a search-result summary of an abstract, which is exactly the kind of second-hand claim that should not be trusted.

TO RESOLVE, in order of value:
1. Read Northwood 1975 itself and record the measured dnu/dT sign with its temperature range.
2. Better, read Schwenk & Wheeler (1978), DOI 10.1016/0022-3115(78)90491-9 — it measures nu DIRECTLY on Zircaloy-4 over 297-589 K, so it settles the sign without going through E and G.
3. Cross-check against NUREG/CR-7024 / PNNL-19417 (Luscher & Geelhood, PNNL, 2011).

Tracked as VAL-3 in crates/outram-park-fork-offbeat/docs/validation/poisson_ratio_zircaloy.md and as GAP-7 in the sibling References.md.

Do NOT change the correlation numerics on the strength of this bead alone. If the sign is genuinely wrong upstream, the workspace rule is to REPRODUCE the defect and document it with a test that pins the discrepancy — not to silently correct it.

---

It survived only in the local v1 store, which diverged from origin's migrated v2 store. Preserved at ref refs/beads/local-preserve-20260812. Original status at preservation: open.
title: Zircaloy Poisson: possible WRONG SIGN in dnu/dT -- highest priority check

acceptance_criteria: Power decays to zero then re-criticality at roughly 8 h; peak fuel and RPV temperatures within digitisation error of the published curves. Docs state 'digitised from published figures' with the citation and the digitiser calibration record.
description:
Reproduce the HTTR 9 MW gas-circulator-trip loss-of-forced-cooling transient at 30% power.

SOURCE, Tier 3: digitise figures from JNST Vol 51 Issue 11-12 (2014), Takamatsu et al. Same technique already used for Kieffer 1977 in TAMPINES, and the workspace has kovan-digitise for exactly this - use the CLI path, not eyeballing.

WHAT ACTUALLY GOVERNS THE RESULT, per the maintainer: reactivity performance sets the converging power level and hence fuel temperature; graphite conduction and RPV-to-cavity radiation set the temperature transient. FORCED CONVECTION IS ABSENT BY DEFINITION - so helium properties matter far less here than conduction and radiation. Do not over-invest in the gas path for this case.

WATCH: xenon reactivity temperature dependence has been the subject of dedicated sensitivity studies. Expect it to matter.

Depends on the RCCS/cavity path (op-jyyp.7) and PRKE feedback (op-juve).
title: HTGR Phase 4.3: HTTR LOFC transient (Tier 3, digitised from figures)

description:
The 160 W/(m2 K) pebble-to-helium coefficient is invented. Wiring KTA friction (op-szmi.8) surfaced a quantitative check on it: at that value the bed sits 204.7 K above bulk helium, against Gao & Shi 2002 Table 2's PEAK fuel-to-coolant difference of 100.7 K at 100% load (918.7 / 876.7 / 818 degC max fuel / fuel-surface / coolant). A bed AVERAGE must be below the peak, so the coefficient is low by roughly 2-3x.

Left unchanged deliberately during op-szmi.8 -- re-anchoring is a modelling decision needing its own V&V, not a side effect of wiring friction.

Route: KTA 3102.2 Nu correlation, transcribed in docs/reactor-scoping/htr10-plant-data.md 7.3. NOTE the OCR caveat on one symbol recorded there -- verify against the source before trusting the transcription.
title: htgr_sim_v1: re-anchor pebble-to-helium HTC against Gao & Shi Table 2

description:
Umbrella for generalizing the ciet_educational_simulator_v2 'app builder' pattern into
outram-park-digital-twin-engine's app_scaffold/ so every current and future real-time
simulator (htgr_sim_v1, fhr_sim_v2, ipwr_sim_v1, abwr_sim_v1, CIET v3, ...) can build on
shared, tested infrastructure instead of hand-rolling its own. Four pieces surveyed
2026-08-17:

1. Physics loop + real-time pacing: app_scaffold already has SharedState<T>,
   spawn_physics_thread_monitored, and RealTimePacer, consumed by htgr_sim_v1/fhr_sim_v2.
   ciet_educational_simulator_v2 hand-rolls its own version (educational_ciet_loop_version_4
   in full_simulation/mod.rs, mirrored in nat_circ_simulation/mod.rs) with fast_forward /
   slow_motion toggles and a timestep_seconds dt-shrink control app_scaffold doesn't have,
   plus one branch (grow timestep back to max on overrun) that actively contradicts
   RealTimePacer's own documented pacing invariant. See child .3.
2. Plot/graph sampling loop: three near-duplicate bounded-history implementations exist
   (HTGR's own Vec+remove(0), and a shared CIET-v1-derived lineage in both
   ciet_educational_simulator_v2 and fhr_sim_v2 that rebuilds a whole 4000-element Vec
   per sample). See child .1.
3. CSV logging: does not exist as real file I/O anywhere in this crate today -- CIET v2's
   "csv" pages are an on-screen scrollable text label, not a file writer. Needs building
   new. See child .2.
4. OPC-UA server/client: already generalized. src/opcua_core/ (op-szmi.1, Done) provides
   enum-dispatched OpcuaSimulator/OpcuaVariable traits + a generic server/PKI/discovery
   layer; src/ciet_opcua/ is the worked reference implementation. src/htgr_opcua/ has its
   node maps/state but isn't wired to opcua_core yet -- that's the existing op-szmi.4
   bead, not new shared-infra work. See child .4.

Survey done by three parallel read-only agents 2026-08-17, no code changed by the survey.
title: app_scaffold: reusable real-time simulator infrastructure (physics loop, plotting, CSV, OPC-UA)

description:
PARTIALLY RESOLVED 2026-08-12 in tampines-steam-tables (the coolprop half is the sibling agent's).

FIXED for TampinesSteamArray: added `set_inlet_mass_flowrate` / `clear_inlet_mass_flowrate` (additive API, no signature changes), implementing OpenFOAM's flowRateInletVelocity. The inlet velocity is re-derived every pressure corrector from the SAME interpolated inlet-face density that then multiplies it to form the boundary mass flux, so the imposed flux is exactly m_dot by construction. `set_inlet_velocity` clears it and vice versa, so the two cannot silently fight over the same patch.

MEASURED (test `prescribed_inlet_mass_flowrate_is_imposed_exactly`), 8 cells, 4 MPa water, target 3.2 kg/s:
  prescribed mass-flow inlet : 3.200000000 kg/s (+0.0000%)
  velocity from CORRECT rho  : 3.200148121 kg/s (+0.0046%)
  velocity from WRONG rho    : 2.583169047 kg/s (-19.2760%)

STILL OPEN: `set_mass_flowrate` itself remains inert bookkeeping. It was deliberately NOT made active -- doing so would silently change behaviour for existing callers who set it for bookkeeping, which is a behavioural breaking change on a published crate. Its doc comment now says plainly that it is not a boundary condition and points at set_inlet_mass_flowrate. Whether to deprecate or repurpose it is a maintainer call.
title: Fluid arrays have no mass-flow boundary condition; velocity BC lets the solved flow drift from the metered one
